title: Argo Rollouts: supported deploy steps
description: The step types a flow definition/pipeline stage targeting an Argo Rollouts environment may use. Discriminated by `type`.

oneOf.title: Canary deploy
oneOf.description: Deploys the named services to the Argo Rollouts environment using a canary strategy, rolling each service's Rollout up to its first pause gate and leaving it parked there. The driver writes the canary steps into the service's Rollout manifest, generating them from this step's weight and those of the canary.promote steps that follow: one traffic weight per step, each gated by an indefinite pause the following canary.promote clears. Any steps the manifest already carried are replaced; the rest of its canary block, traffic routing and analysis templates and service references and surge bounds, is left as authored. Because the driver owns the step indexes, a manifest that authors `analysis.startingStep` is refused rather than silently pointed at a different rung. A service reaching 100 in this step alone has no gate to park at, so a lone canary.deploy deploys it to completion. Exactly one canary.deploy opens a service's canary in an environment, and the canary.promote steps that follow climb it; a second canary.deploy for the same service and environment is refused. Timing between increments belongs to the flow, not the Argo controller: put a wait step between the steps that should be separated in time.

environment.description: The environment id this step targets; join key into the top-level environments map and flow_definition.environments.

services.description: The services this step deploys. At least one is required, and each is named at most once: a step naming one service twice is refused.

name.description: Name of the service to deploy, matching a service defined for this environment.

weight.description: Traffic weight this canary increment deploys to, and the first rung of the ladder the driver generates for the service. Taken together, a service's canary weights in one environment must never decrease, must end at 100, and must all differ, since a repeated weight cannot identify a single gate; a flow whose weights cannot describe a gradual rollout to full traffic is refused before it reads, commits or syncs anything. May later become an object to express other kinds of weight (e.g. scale, replicas).

oneOf.title: Canary promote
oneOf.description: Advances services' canary Rollouts one increment: for each named service, this step clears the pause gate that takes its Rollout to the given weight, then waits until the resulting increment completes or reaches the next gate. A canary with K pauses uses K canary.promote steps, one per gate, in ascending weight order. Each must follow that service's canary.deploy in the same environment; a canary.promote for a service and environment no canary.deploy opened is refused up front rather than failing in flight against a Rollout that was never deployed. Because the gate is derived from the step's weight rather than from where the Rollout currently sits, re-running a canary.promote that already succeeded is a no-op, and running one out of order fails rather than skipping an increment.

environment.description: The environment id this step targets; join key into the top-level environments map and flow_definition.environments.

services.description: The services this step promotes. At least one is required, and each is named at most once: a step naming one service twice is refused.

name.description: Name of the service to promote, matching a service defined for this environment.

weight.description: Traffic weight this promotion advances to; it is a rung of the ladder the service's canary.deploy generated, and it selects which pause gate to clear. The minimum is 1, unlike canary.deploy's 0: a promotion to 0 shifts no traffic, so it advances nothing, while a canary.deploy at 0 legitimately brings a canary up alongside the stable version to be smoke tested before any traffic moves. Taken together, a service's canary weights in one environment must never decrease, must end at 100, and must all differ, since a repeated weight cannot identify a single gate; a flow whose weights cannot describe a gradual rollout to full traffic is refused before it reads, commits or syncs anything. May later become an object to express other kinds of weight (e.g. scale, replicas).
